newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Manuel plans cut in state spending.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Manuel plans cut in state spending.

text.p: South Africa is committed to real state spending cuts to reduce its budget deficit, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said in an interview published on Sunday.

Manuel told Business Times newspaper he would rely on "a real cut in state expenditure" to achieve a budgeted deficit of four percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in the 1997/8 financial year and three percent over the following two years.
"There is a lot of scepticism about our ability to deliver a four percent deficit, but that figure is non-negotiable," he said.
Manuel ruled out tax increases, saying that the spending cuts would have to be accompanied by improved tax collection in order to achieve the targeted deficits.
Reports last year said the cabinet was committed to a 185 billion rand ($39.5 billion) budget for the 1997/98 financial year (April to March).
At an inflation rate of nine percent, this would mean spending cuts of two percent in real terms.

The Business Times quoted Manuel as saying the cuts would be achieved through a series of efficiencies, including reform of state procurement, improved cash and debt management and a medium-term expenditure budget.
The finance minister also said his government did not want to rely on "roll-overs" of unspent budget allocations to achieve the deficit targets.
Manuel was cautious about South Africa's economic growth prospects.
"The economy will be hard-pressed to meet the targeted 2.9 percent growth. The (central) Reserve Bank's 2.5 percent estimate seems closer to mark," he told the paper.
